'''Guido Altarelli''' (12 July 1941<ref name="Maiani Martinelli pp. 1–15">{{cite journal | last=Maiani | first=Luciano | last2=Martinelli | first2=Guido | title=Guido Altarelli | journal=[[Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science]] | publisher=Annual Reviews | volume=68 | issue=1 | date=19 Oct 2018 | issn=0163-8998 | doi=10.1146/annurev-nucl-101917-021029 | pages=1–15| bibcode=2018ARNPS..68....1M | doi-access=free }}</ref> – 30 September 2015<ref>{{cite journal | title = Guido Altarelli (1941 - 2015) | journal = CERN Bulletin  | volume = 901 | issue = 41 & 42, Mon 05 Oct | pages = 249 |year=2015 | url =https://cds.cern.ch/record/2056743| bibcode = 2015NuPhB.901..249F | last1 = Forte | first1 = Stefano | last2 = Ridolfi | first2 = Giovanni | doi = 10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2015.10.021 | doi-access = free }}</ref>) was an Italian theoretical physicist.<ref name="Forte 2019 p. ">{{cite book | last=Forte | first=Stefano | title=From my vast repertoire-- : Guido Altarelli's legacy | publisher=World Scientific Publishing Co. Pte. Ltd | location=Singapore | year=2019 | isbn=978-981-323-804-6 | oclc=1061311069 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Maiani, Luciano|author-link=Luciano Maiani|author2=Parisi, Giorgio|author-link2=Giorgio Parisi|title=Obituary. Guido Altarelli|journal=Physics Today|date=March 2016|page= 65|doi=10.1063/pt.3.3114|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Biography==
Altarelli graduated in Physics from the [[Sapienza University of Rome]] in 1963 with [[:it:Raoul Gatto|Raoul Gatto]] whom he followed to the [[University of Florence]] (1965–68).  He held positions at New York University (1968–69), the [[Rockefeller University]] (New York, 1969–70), the [[École Normale Superieure]] in Paris (1976–77, 81) and [[Boston University]] (1985–86).  In 1970-92 he held a faculty position at the Sapienza University of Rome (full professor of theoretical physics since 1980).  He was Director of the Rome Section of the INFN (1985–87).  In 1992 he moved to the newly established [[University of Roma Tre]].<ref>{{cite web| title = The title of the IFJ PAN Honorary Professor conferred on Guido Altarelli| url = http://www.ifj.edu.pl/wyd/prof_altarelli/?lang=en| date = September 16, 2013| access-date = March 12, 2014| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151001215841/http://www.ifj.edu.pl/wyd/prof_altarelli/?lang=en| archive-date = October 1, 2015| url-status = dead}}</ref>

In 1987-2006 he was a Senior Staff Physicist at the Theory Division of [[CERN]], and was Theory Division Leader from 2000-04. At CERN he had a leading role in the interpretation of SppS results, in the preparation of LEP and the LHC and in the theoretical analysis of the experimental results.

In 2011 Altarelli gave a talk ''The Mystery of Neutrino Mixing'' at the international symposium on subnuclear physics held in Vatican City.<ref>{{cite book|editor=Sánchez Sorondo, Marcelo|editor-link=Marcelo Sánchez Sorondo|editor2=Zichichi, Antonino|editor-link2=Antonino Zichichi|chapter=''The Mystery of Neutrino Mixing'' by Guido Altarelli|pages=218–228|title=Subnuclear Physics: Past, Present and Future; Proceedings of the International Symposium, held 30 October - 2 November 2011, held in Vatican City|series=Scripta Varia, volume 119|publisher=[[Pontifical Academy of Sciences]]|year=2014|chapter-url=https://www.pas.va/content/dam/casinapioiv/pas/pdf-volumi/scripta-varia/sv119/sv119-altarelli.pdf}}</ref>

His best known contribution, obtained with [[Giorgio Parisi]] in 1977, is the derivation of the [[Quantum chromodynamics|QCD]] evolution equations for parton densities, known as the Altarelli- Parisi or [[DGLAP]] equations.<ref>{{cite journal | author = G. Altarelli and G. Parisi | title = Asymptotic Freedom in Parton Language | journal = Nuclear Physics  | volume = B126 | issue = 2 | pages = 298–318 | year = 1977 | doi= 10.1016/0550-3213(77)90384-4| bibcode = 1977NuPhB.126..298A }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ansa.it/scienza/notizie/rubriche/ricerca/2015/10/01/morto-il-fisico-guido-altarelli_4556d352-57d4-4f3c-9a6e-9449ba3d4bca.html|title=Morto il fisico Guido Altarelli|work=ANSA.it|language=it|date=October 2015}}</ref>

==Awards==
* Member of the Polish Academy of Sciences<ref>{{cite journal|title=Faces and places: Polish institute makes Guido Altarelli honorary professor|journal=CERN Courier|date=December 2013|volume=53|issue=10|page=33|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1734902}}</ref>
* 2011: Julius Wess Award for Outstanding Achievements in Elementary Particle and Astroparticle Physics - The Karlsruhe Institute of Technology<ref name="CERN Bulletin">{{cite journal|last1=Schaeffer|first1=Anaïs|title=I can't wait to find out what Nature has in store for us|journal=CERN Bulletin|date=February 2012|volume=06-07|url=https://cds.cern.ch/journal/CERNBulletin/2012/07/News%20Articles/1421253}}</ref>
* 2012: [[J. J. Sakurai Prize for Theoretical Particle Physics]] - The American Physical Society<ref name="CERN Bulletin" />
* 2015: [[High Energy and Particle Physics Prize]] - [[European Physical Society|EPS]] HEPP Prize<ref>{{Cite web |last=High Energy Particle Physics Division of EPS |title=High Energy Particle Physics Prize |url=https://eps-hepp.web.cern.ch/hepp-prize-awards.php |access-date=2026-02-07 |website=eps-hepp.web.cern.ch}}</ref>
